content: If you suspect you are experiencing a side effect from a medication, contact your healthcare provider immediately. You can also report side effects to the FDA through their MedWatch program at www.fda.gov/medwatch or by calling 800-FDA-1088. In Canada, you can report side effects to Health Canada at www.canada.ca/medeffect or by calling 866-234-2345. Serious Side Effects of Dexlansoprazole Kidney Problems Dexlansoprazole can cause a kidney condition called acute tubulointerstitial nephritis, which may occur at any time during treatment. If you notice a reduction in the amount of urine you produce or see blood in your urine, contact your doctor immediately. Antibiotic-Associated Diarrhea Treatment with dexlansoprazole can lead to an overgrowth of bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) in the gut. Symptoms include watery diarrhea, diarrhea that does not resolve, blood in the stool, severe stomach cramps, or fever that begins after starting or finishing the medication. If you experience any of these symptoms, contact your healthcare provider immediately. Severe Skin Reactions Dexlansoprazole can cause life-threatening skin reactions such as Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) and Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN). If you develop a rash, stop taking the medication and contact your healthcare provider immediately. Seek emergency medical attention if you experience painful red or purple skin that looks burned and peels, flat red rashes or blisters on the skin, mouth, nose, or genitals, or red, painful, watery eyes. Severe Allergic Reaction (DRESS) Dexlansoprazole can cause a rare but serious allergic reaction called Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS), also known as multi-organ hypersensitivity. This reaction can affect multiple organs, including the liver, kidneys, and heart. Stop taking the medication and seek immediate medical attention if you experience symptoms such as a skin rash, hives, fever, swollen lymph nodes, shortness of breath, swelling in the feet or legs, dark urine, or yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice). Lupus Dexlansoprazole may trigger or worsen lupus, an autoimmune condition where the immune system attacks the body’s own tissues. Notify your healthcare provider if you develop new or worsening joint pain or a rash on your arms or cheeks. Vitamin B-12 Deficiency Long-term use of dexlansoprazole (three years or more) can reduce the absorption of vitamin B-12, leading to deficiency. Symptoms include a sore tongue, weakness, or tingling/numbness in the hands or feet. If you experience these symptoms, stop taking the medication and contact your healthcare provider. Hypomagnesemia Dexlansoprazole can cause low magnesium levels (hypomagnesemia), which can lead to serious complications such as seizures or heart rhythm problems. People taking the medication long-term or in combination with other drugs that lower magnesium levels are at higher risk. Symptoms include changes in heart rate or rhythm, dizziness, muscle spasms, or seizures. Stop taking the medication and contact your healthcare provider if you experience these symptoms. Bone Loss and Fractures Long-term use of dexlansoprazole, especially in older adults or at high doses, may increase the risk of bone loss and fractures. Severe Allergic Reactions Dexlansoprazole may cause serious allergic reactions. Stop taking the medication and seek immediate medical attention if you experience breathing difficulties, wheezing, a racing heart, fever, swollen lymph nodes, swelling of the face, lips, mouth, tongue, or throat, trouble swallowing, throat tightness, itching, skin rash, hives, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, or fainting. Precautions: Who Should Not Use Dexlansoprazole? Allergies to Ingredients Do not use dexlansoprazole if you are allergic to: Dexlansoprazole Dexilant or Kapidex Any other proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) Any ingredients in the specific product dispensed. Your pharmacist can provide a full list of ingredients. Drug Interactions Dexlansoprazole should not be taken with certain medications. Inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter (OTC) medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are using. Specific medications to discuss include: Methotrexate Digoxin (used for irregular heartbeat or heart failure) Warfarin (a blood thinner) Tacrolimus (used to prevent organ transplant rejection) Certain antiretroviral medications for HIV/AIDS, such as rilpivirine, nelfinavir, or saquinavir St. John’s Wort Rifampin (used for tuberculosis) Some medications may alter the blood levels of dexlansoprazole or vice versa. Always inform your healthcare provider about all medications you are taking. Important Usage Information Only take dexlansoprazole if it has been prescribed to you by a healthcare provider. Follow the prescribed dosage and instructions. Do not share this medication with others, even if they have the same condition. Keep the medication out of reach of children. Do not chew, cut, or crush the capsules. If you have difficulty swallowing, you may open the capsule and sprinkle the contents on one tablespoon of applesauce. Swallow the mixture immediately without mixing it with other foods. If administered through a nasogastric (NG) tube, follow your healthcare provider’s instructions. Dexlansoprazole is not intended for immediate relief of heartburn. It may take 1 to 4 days to take full effect. Children under 2 years of age may be at greater risk for certain side effects. Discuss the risks with your healthcare provider. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding It is not known if dexlansoprazole can harm an unborn baby. Inform your healthcare provider if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It is not known if dexlansoprazole passes into breast milk. Inform your healthcare provider if you are breastfeeding or planning to breastfeed. Overdose If you or someone else has taken too much dexlansoprazole, seek medical help immediately. Call 911 or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. Missed Dose If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. Do not take double or extra doses. Food and Drink Interactions There are no known interactions between dexlansoprazole and foods or drinks. It is also unknown if alcohol consumption affects the medication. Always consult your healthcare provider for guidance.
